B. Is this measure already running in Satakunta wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure lead to lung cancer being found at an earlier stage, and by how much?
Measure: Symptom awareness campaign (cough over three weeks). A campaign on the English "Be Clear on Cancer" model telling people with a persistent cough to see a doctor. Weak evidence: in England the share found at stage I rose during the campaign months and faded within months, so it has to be repeated every year, and the extra GP visits and chest X-rays cost several times the advertising.
supported_en: British Journal of Cancer 2015: the English campaign raised GP visits for cough among people aged 50+ by 63% over the 8 weeks around the campaign.
not_supported_en: The passages I read did not show the 3.1-point rise in stage I, or the 0.8-point yearly average we assume.
summary_en: B: I found no public sign of a cough awareness campaign. Satakunnan hyvinvointialue (11.11.2026) runs a pathway that lets health centres send people with symptoms such as a long-lasting cough, plus at least 20 pack-years of smoking, straight to chest CT; it started as a pilot in early 2022, became standard in 2024, and about 170 patients have been scanned. A: The British Journal of Cancer evaluation (2015) found the English campaign raised GP visits for cough among people aged 50+ by 63%, but the passages I read did not show the stage I figure.
unanswered_en: Searches with several Finnish terms found no Satakunta or Tyks campaign page, and I did not reach the stage-shift figures in the article.
